title: Two or more months late now predicts default
discovery: Clients two or more months late on the latest statement defaulted at 69.5%. The portfolio rate is 22.1%.
evidence: 3,129 clients; 2,176 defaults; 3.1 times the portfolio default rate. This is an observed group rate, not an individual prediction. facts: default-rate-pay1-late2plus, count-pay1-late2plus, default-rate-overall.
recommendation: Review accounts that are two or more months late on the latest statement.
headlineLabel: default when two or more months late on the latest statement

title: Both inactive and over-limit cards default more
discovery: Default rates are higher at both ends of average utilization: 34.9% at 0% or below and 34.2% above 100%.
evidence: Six-month average utilization bands: 34.9% at 0% or below (n = 1,041), 16.6% at 0-25% (n = 13,310), 19.9% at 25-50% (n = 4,555), 28.1% at 50-100% (n = 10,422), and 34.2% above 100% (n = 637). These are observed group rates. facts: default-rate-avg-utilization-le0, default-rate-avg-utilization-gt0-le0-25, default-rate-avg-utilization-gt0-25-le0-5, default-rate-avg-utilization-gt0-5-le1, default-rate-avg-utilization-gt1, default-rate-overall.
recommendation: Review inactive accounts and over-limit accounts separately; both sit well above the portfolio rate.

title: Each late month adds risk
discovery: Default rates rose across the late-month counts, from 11.7% with none to 70.3% with all six.
evidence: 3,743 clients had three or more late months and defaulted at 60.0%. Counts describe the six observed statements. facts: default-rate-months-delayed-0, default-rate-months-delayed-1, default-rate-months-delayed-2, default-rate-months-delayed-3, default-rate-months-delayed-4, default-rate-months-delayed-5, default-rate-months-delayed-6, default-rate-months-delayed-ge3.
recommendation: Count late months when prioritizing repayment reviews.

title: Delaying personas hold most defaults
discovery: Persistent delayers and occasional delayers account for 61.5% of all defaults among 30.5% of clients.
evidence: Persistent delayers: 2,589 clients, 1,658 defaults, 64.0% default rate; Transactors: 9,031 clients, 1,125 defaults, 12.5% default rate; Occasional delayers: 6,555 clients, 2,420 defaults, 36.9% default rate; Revolvers, never late: 11,790 clients, 1,427 defaults, 12.1% default rate. The two delaying personas account for 30.5% of clients and 61.5% of defaults; they hold 2.0x their share of defaults. These are descriptive group rates, not individual predictions. facts: share-of-defaults-delayers, share-of-clients-delayers, default-rate-cluster-0, default-rate-cluster-1, default-rate-cluster-2, default-rate-cluster-3.
recommendation: Review persistent delayers first, then occasional delayers, using each client's repayment history.
headlineLabel: of defaults come from the 30.5% of clients who delay

title: Low credit limits carry the most default
discovery: The lowest credit-limit quarter defaulted at 31.8%. The highest quarter defaulted at 14.0%.
evidence: 7,673 clients in the lowest quarter. Quartile default rates: 31.8%, 24.7%, 17.4%, 14.0%. facts: default-rate-limit-q1, default-rate-limit-q2, default-rate-limit-q3, default-rate-limit-q4.
recommendation: Review repayment history alongside the credit limit.

title: Small payments signal default
discovery: The lowest latest-payment quarter defaulted at 31.7%. The highest quarter defaulted at 13.8%.
evidence: 7,805 clients in the lowest quarter. Quartile default rates by latest payment amount (PAY_AMT1): 31.7%, 22.1%, 20.5%, 13.8%. The amount is a single-statement figure; it does not establish consecutive low-payment statements. facts: default-rate-payment-amount-q1, default-rate-payment-amount-q2, default-rate-payment-amount-q3, default-rate-payment-amount-q4.
recommendation: Review clients whose latest payment falls in the lowest quarter alongside their repayment history.

title: Higher payment ratios go with lower default rates
discovery: Higher six-month aggregate payment-ratio quartiles had lower observed default rates: 29.2%, 26.2%, 17.9%, 15.3%.
evidence: The lowest quartile has 7,493 clients; the highest has 7,491. PAY_RATIO divides six-month payments by positive bills (denominator at least 1), capped at 5. This association does not show that increasing payments causes lower default. facts: default-rate-payment-ratio-q1, default-rate-payment-ratio-q2, default-rate-payment-ratio-q3, default-rate-payment-ratio-q4.
recommendation: Review the six-month aggregate payment ratio with delay history.

title: Age matters only at the edges
discovery: Clients aged 30-39 had the lowest age-band default rate, 20.3%. Clients aged 60 or more had the highest, 28.3%.
evidence: Age 30-39: 11,226 clients. Age 60+: only 339 clients, so the estimate is less precise. These are descriptive group differences. facts: default-rate-age-le29, default-rate-age-30-39, default-rate-age-40-49, default-rate-age-50-59, default-rate-age-60-plus.
recommendation: Compare confidence intervals and use age bands for fairness checks.

title: Demographic default rates differ
discovery: Education default rates span 18.1 percentage points including Other. Married clients defaulted at 23.5%, single clients at 20.9%.
evidence: Graduate school 19.2% (n=10,563); University 23.7% (n=14,019); High school 25.2% (n=4,915); Other education 7.1% (n=468). Married 23.5% (n=13,643); Single 20.9% (n=15,945); Other status 23.6% (n=377). Male 24.2% (n=11,874); Female 20.8% (n=18,091). These unadjusted comparisons do not measure causal effects. facts: default-rate-education-graduate, default-rate-education-university, default-rate-education-highschool, default-rate-education-other, default-rate-marriage-married, default-rate-marriage-single, default-rate-marriage-other, default-rate-sex-male, default-rate-sex-female.
recommendation: Use demographic comparisons for fairness checks alongside repayment evidence.

title: The risk tier rule separates clients well
discovery: An engineered tier built from the delay features and average utilization has default rates of Low 10.9%, Medium 15.7%, High 45.2%.
evidence: The High tier has 8,713 clients. The tier reuses worst delay, late-month count and average utilization; it is not independent evidence beyond those inputs. facts: default-rate-risk-tier-low, default-rate-risk-tier-medium, default-rate-risk-tier-high.
recommendation: Use the engineered tier as a summary and inspect its input features.
